subject: Linguistics
title: Isolating Languages
description: A quick win: understand Isolating Languages.

hook.text: In Vietnamese every word is one morpheme, one syllable—no affixes anywhere.

buildup.text: Isolating languages keep morphemes separate; grammar comes from word order and particles.

discovery.text: Mandarin is largely isolating: 'I yesterday go store' uses position, not endings, for grammar.

twist.text: No language is purely isolating—even Mandarin has some compounds and a few affixes.

climax.text: Isolating languages prove that rich morphology is optional—word order can do the heavy lifting.

punchline.text: One word, one meaning, no extras needed.

quiz.question: What defines an isolating language?
options: Each word is typically one morpheme
